newsitem.title: USA: Brazil port fire not "big event" for exports - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Brazil port fire not "big event" for exports - USDA.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait Thursday said a recent fire at Brazil's Paranagua port would only modestly reduce soybean exports from that port for a week to 10 days.
"It's not going to be a big event in terms of the overall capacity of Brazil to export," Goldthwait said in an interview with USDA Radio.
He said the fire, which shut down one of five conveyor belts at the export terminal, may reduce the rate of loading of soybeans by about 5,000 tonnes for between seven and 10 days.
Goldthwait said the level of exports by Brazil at this time of year can be as much as 600,000 to 800,000 tonnes a month.
Earlier this week, CBOT soybean futures soared on ideas that the small fire at the key port would slow Brazil exports and encourage world buyers to purchase U.S. supplies.
